title: Choose the visual world for ORT Server
question: The roll assigned Mission Manual. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mission Manual
options.lineage: NASA Graphics Standards Manual (1975) and mission flight-plan documents, via the Apoapsis orbit
options.thesis: Every run is a mission with a flight plan, set like a standards manual: white sheets, one crimson, a strict grid.
materials: neo-grotesk set on a visible 8px grid
options.viewport: Ink left rail, white work sheet; the run's flight plan spans the top as a timed trajectory strip in ORT job colours, findings set large in the grid below, dense tables after.
options.risk: Turns cold and bureaucratic if the trajectory strip is timid or the type scale is flat.

raised.raise: Triage gives one finding the whole detail pane with the next one preloaded, stepped with J and K.
Strict ink semantics: each colour means one thing; crimson marks only the brand and the current position.
Every rule is a 1px hairline and states are marks: resolved findings are struck through, not boxed.
One modular grid every table, panel and chart snaps to; layouts reflow by whole columns.
Hierarchy by type scale and weight, never by stat-card tiles.

options.label: Transit Line
options.lineage: Vignelli’s 1972 New York subway diagram and the Unimark signage system
options.thesis: The ORT pipeline is a transit line: each worker is a line colour, each job a station, every screen signed like a platform.
materials: black signage bands with white bold grotesk
45/90 degree line diagrams with station discs
options.viewport: A black sign band names the repository and run; below it the run is drawn as a line diagram, analyzer to reporter, with findings counts at each station; tables follow.
options.risk: Pipeline-as-subway is a familiar trope; it reads themed if the sign bands spread beyond headers.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: A graphite working surface with hairline seams, persistent panels and syntax-derived state colours.
materials: hairline panel seams, one elevation step
options.viewport: Tiled persistent panels: run list, run detail, finding inspector; destructive actions isolated.
options.case: Developers recognise it at once and it is dense; it loses on long OSPO reading sessions and sits close to the dark terminal you ruled out.
options.risk: Drifts toward the hacker-terminal costume you asked to avoid.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the viewport; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: One finding per screen with a right rail of actions.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reviewers compare many findings at once, not one per screen.
options.kept: One finding owns the detail pane, next one preloaded (J/K).

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed terrain colour language with the course in reserved purple.
options.viewport: Dependency terrain with the review path overprinted.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither user group reads their work as terrain.
options.kept: One meaning per colour; one reserved colour for the current position.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.lineage: ruled reference editions with a centre key rail
options.thesis: Two dense columns around a rail of keys, apparatus in a wide margin.
options.viewport: Licence texts set as an annotated edition.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reading edition fights dense finding tables.
options.kept: 1px hairlines everywhere; states as marks, resolved is struck through.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid is visible and the page is its proof.
options.viewport: A poster-scale grid with monumental counts.
options.case: Fuses poorly: poster scale wastes the dense screen.
options.kept: One modular grid every element snaps to.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.viewport: Giant numerals with tiny mono labels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in the product is about letterforms.
options.kept: Hierarchy by type scale, not by cards.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light dashboard like GitHub, Snyk or Sentry, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, tabbed run page, summary row and finding tables.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other security dashboard by design.
